title: In Vitro Selection of Engineered Transcriptional Repressors for Targeted Epigenetic Silencing
protocol: Engineer a fluorescence-based reporter cell line to monitor the transcriptional activity of the target gene by flow cytometry.
Identify cell lines expressing the target gene to be silenced.
Browse the target gene to be silenced in the Human Protein Atlas and navigate through its "Cell line" section to identify those lines representative of the somatic tissue of interest.
Alternatively, interrogate a publicly available RNA sequencing (RNA-Seq) database.
Among the candidates, prioritize cell lines for which efficient transient gene delivery protocols are available.
Choose nucleofection as it ensures high transfection efficiencies.
Select human erythroleukemia K-562 cells to generate a cell line reporting the transcriptional activity of the beta-2-microglobulin (B2M) gene.
Prioritize candidates to avoid cell lines in which the target gene is essential for cell viability.
Generate a genetic disruption control by transfecting cells with Cas9 nuclease and a gRNA targeting one of the first coding exons of the gene.
Identify the target splicing isoform preferentially used in the selected cell line.
Select a gRNA that can cut effectively and specifically in the first coding exon of the target isoform.
Transfect 1 µg of spCas9-encoding plasmid (hCas9) and 250 ng of gRNA-encoding plasmid (phU6-gRNA) per 5 × 10^5 cells through nucleofection.
Culture K-562 cells at 37 °C under 5% CO2 in RPMI-1640 supplemented with 10% fetal bovine serum [FBS], L-glutamine, and penicillin/streptomycin [100 U/mL].
Monitor levels of gene disruption over time using a mutation detection kit (follow the manufacturer's instructions).
Clone a donor template for homologous recombination-mediated integration of a fluorescent reporter under the transcriptional control of the target gene.
Identify the region of the target gene to integrate the fluorophore expression cassette.
Avoid targeting transcriptionally relevant elements such as CpG islands and regions enriched for H3K27 acetylation.
If the target gene does not encode for a secreted protein, fuse the reporter to the last codon of the target gene through a 2A self-cleaving peptide.
Place the reporter in an intronic region of the target gene.
Force integration through a splice acceptor site and internal ribosome entry sequence to impair target gene functionality.
Use Chopchop to select gRNA cutting at the 5′-AGGCTACTAGCCCCATCAAGAGG-3′ sequence of the first B2M intron.
Design a donor template with a left homology arm, promoter-free transgene expression cassette (SA-3X Stop Codon-IRES-tdTomato-BGH poly(A)), and right homology arm.
Ensure homology arms are appropriately sized for effective homologous recombination in the specific cell type.
Deliver the CRISPR/Cas9 nuclease system and the donor template into the target cell line.
Transfect 1 µg of spCas9-encoding plasmid, 250 ng of gRNA-encode plasmid, and 1 µg of donor template-encoding plasmid per 5 × 10^5 K-562 cells through nucleofection.
Culture the transfected cells for at least 14 days.
Monitor expression levels of the fluorescent reporter over time using a flow cytometer.
Activate the phycoerythrin (PE) channel to measure fluorescence intensity of the tdTomato reporter.
Sort single tdTomato-positive K-562 cells through FACS into individual wells of a 96-well plate.
Screen reporter-positive clones by PCR after cell expansion in culture.
Extract genomic DNA from 1 × 105 cells per reporter-positive clone using a DNA extraction kit.
Amplify the B2M target region with forward primer 5'-GTATTTGCTGGTTATGTTAG-3' and reverse primer 5'-AATGGTTGAGTTGGAC-3'.
Analyze the PCR product using 1% agarose gel electrophoresis.
Screen for clones showing the band related to integration of tdTomato in the B2M target locus (3,413 bp).
Exclude clones with a band related to the wild-type target locus (1,027 bp).
Transform plasmids encoding for the ETRs in chemically competent E. coli cells following the manufacturer's instructions.
Screen colonies for the presence of the ETR-bearing plasmid by restriction enzyme digestion and Sanger sequencing.
Choose one positive colony for plasmid DNA Midiprep production following the manufacturer's instructions.
Clone gRNAs inside the phU6-gRNA backbone using molecular biology design software.
Append a 5'-CACCG-3' sequence upstream of the protospacer to generate a 25 nt-long oligo referred as SGfw.
Generate another 25 nt-long oligo referred as SGrv by appending a 5'-AAAC-3' sequence and a 5'-C-3' downstream of the reverse complement of the protospacer of the selected gRNA.
Order both the SGfw and SGrv sequences as salt-free single-stranded DNA oligos, resuspended in water at 100 µM.
Add 1 µL of each oligo to 2 µL of annealing buffer.
Add 16 µL of water to the solution.
Place the solution in a thermocycler programmed to start at 95 °C for 10 min.
Gradually cool the solution to 25 °C over 45 min.
Dilute 1 µL of the annealed oligos with 99 µL of nuclease-free water.
Ligate 1 µL of this dilution with 50 ng of phU6-gRNA plasmid previously digested with BsaI restriction enzyme.
Transform 20 µL of chemically competent E. coli cells with 2 µL of the ligation product.
Pick multiple colonies for plasmid DNA miniprep production.
Control the successful cloning of the protospacer by Sanger sequencing using a primer matching to the U6 promoter.
Choose one of the positive colonies for plasmid DNA midiprep production.
Prepare separate tubes containing 500 ng of each of the dCas9:KRAB-, dCas9:DNMT3A-, and dCas9:DNMT3L-encoding plasmids.
Add 125 ng of a gRNA-encoding plasmid per tube for the screen.
Include a gRNA- and ETR-free nucleofection condition as mock-treated sample.
Perform the screen with at least three technical replicates per sample.
Pellet 5 × 10^5 B2MTdTomato K-562 cells per tube.
Nucleofect the pelleted cells with the plasmid mix according to the manufacturer's instructions.
Resuspend the nucleofected cells in 200 µL of previously warmed RPMI-1640 mammalian cell culture media.
Place the resuspended cells back into the incubator.
Use flow cytometry to measure the percentage of silenced cells at different time points after delivery of the ETRs.
Set the threshold of reporter-negative cells using wild-type (WT) cells not bearing the fluorophore-coding sequence.
Set the gate for reporter-positive cells using the mock-treated sample.
Include a genetic disruption control in the experiment.
Monitor CRISPR delivery efficiency and cell fitness deprived of the target gene.
Assess both short- (day 3, day 7, day 10) and long-term (day 21, day 35) silencing efficiencies.
Identify top three gRNAs for long-term silencing efficiency.
Select reporter-negative subpopulation stably maintained in samples with the top-performing gRNAs using FACS.
Perform FACS on bulk mock-treated samples to maintain consistent treatment conditions.
Use RNA-seq to evaluate genome-wide transcriptional deregulation upon ETR delivery.
Extract RNA from both reporter-silenced subpopulations and mock-treated cells.
Assess quality and concentration of extracted RNA using commercially available kits.
Perform RNA fragmentation using commercially available kits.
Perform retrotranscription using commercially available kits.
Prepare RNA-seq libraries using commercially available kits.
Quantify library concentration using quality control instruments.
Check library quality using quality control instruments.
Sequence libraries on a next generation sequencer with 100 bp paired-end protocol.
Align read tags to the appropriate reference genome.
Quantify transcript expression using STAR aligner and Rsubread package.
Perform alignment on the tdTomato sequence separately.
Filter genes with at least one count per million (cpm) in at least three samples.
Evaluate differential gene expression using edgeR function glmFit.
Set a threshold of 0.01 on adjusted p values for Benjamini-Hochberg correction.
Evaluate off-target CpG methylation activity by MeDIP-seq.
Extract genomic DNA from samples treated with top three gRNAs and mock-treated cells using commercially available kits.
Sonicate 500 ng of genomic DNA using an ultrasonicator at a duty cycle of 20%, PIP of 175, Cycles per Burst of 200, and Time of 40 seconds.
Prepare sequencing libraries for MeDIP-seq using commercially available kits (following the manufacturers' instructions).
Quantify prepared libraries by fluorometric assay after adaptor ligation step.
Check ligation efficiency by qPCR using commercially available library quantification kits.
Mix randomly-selected libraries to obtain library pools and ensure an equal amount of ng for each library.
Add methylated and unmethylated spike-in control DNA provided in the kit to each pool.
Retain 10% volume of the library as "input" without immunoprecipitation.
Perform immunoprecipitation on the remaining 90% of the library using a monoclonal antibody directed against 5-methylcytosine.
Purify enriched and input libraries using kits for purification of 5-methylcytosine immunoprecipitation product.
Evaluate enrichment efficiency by performing quantitative real-time PCR on internal spike in controls using primers provided with the kit.
Compute enrichment specificity from the recovery of methylated and unmethylated DNA using cycle threshold (Ct) values of MeDIP and input fractions obtained from qPCR reactions.
Consider IP libraries to be successful if specificity values are ≥0.95.
Amplify the libraries using MeDIP-seq library preparation kits following manufacturers' instructions.
Perform quantification and library size distribution analysis of the product.
Perform library sequencing on next generation sequencers with paired-end sequencing, read length of 100 bp, aiming at an average of 30 M reads/sample.
Align sequencing read tags to the appropriate reference genome (e.g., hg38) using bwa (v 0.7.5 or higher).
Identify peaks using MACS (v 2.0.10 or higher), allowing for the identification of broad peaks (-slocal = 0,-llocal = 500000).
Create a common set of regions from different samples using BEDTools' multiintersection tool, enabling the clustering option.
Calculate per-sample coverage over the final region list using BEDTools' multicov, discarding duplicated reads.
Perform analysis of the matrix count using edgeR.
Apply a filter of at least one count per million (cpm) in at least three samples to discard low-enriched regions.
Identify differential methylation by adopting the generalized log-linear model implemented in edgeR and normalizing using conditional quantile normalization to correct for region-wise GC-content.
Select differentially methylized regions by applying a threshold of 0.01 on BH adjusted p values.
Filter MeDIP-seq results for a nominal p value <0.01.
Create two sets of regions: select regions having logFC >1 in the first set and regions having logFC <-1 in the second set.
Retrieve the RepeatMasker annotation for the chosen genome as a bed file.
Count the number of elements in each set.
Convert the count as a ratio over the number of regions for each dataset.
Extract the ratio of methylome that overlaps each class of repeats.
Perform a Chi-squared test to detect any significant enrichment.
Evaluate if differentially transcribed or differentially methylated regions between ETR- and mock-treated samples map to in silico-predicted off-target gRNA binding.
Use CRISPR design suite as the off-target gRNA binding prediction tool.
For every putative off-target region, examine the closest transcription start site (TSS).
For every putative off-target region, examine the closest methylated region.
Consider a region associated with a gene regulated at an FDR <0.01 and within 10 Kb of TSS as a true off-target effect.
Consider a region associated with a methylated region regulated at an FDR <0.01 and within 1 Kb distance as a true off-target effect.
Identify the number and features of regions transcriptionally altered or overmethylated in samples treated with each of the three top-performing gRNAs compared to mock-treated samples.
Rank the potential impact of an off-target site on the physiology of target cells starting from intragenic regulatory region-physiologically expressed gene as the most impacting.
